title: Consolidate AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md into one short file
description: Owner's request (2026-11-12), to be done right after PR #18 and before anything else, as its own PR. AGENTS.md (171 lines) and CLAUDE.md duplicate each other and the Beads boilerplate appears three times; parts contradict this repository's rules (bd dolt push, 'don't bd import'). Make AGENTS.md the single file and CLAUDE.md a one-line @AGENTS.md import. Keep it SHORT: about a quarter of the current length. Just say the project uses Beads (bd prime gives the rest); no tutorial on bd, no 'Non-Interactive Shell Commands' section, no repeated rule blocks. Keep what is specific to this repository: issue sync via .beads/issues.jsonl and the cloud-session 403, build and test commands, architecture overview, conventions (including regenerating every README image when the picture changes). Check that bd setup / bd doctor do not re-insert their blocks.
notes:
AGENTS.md rewritten to 40 lines; CLAUDE.md is a one-line @AGENTS.md import.
bd itself does not rewrite the files; only 'bd setup claude|codex' would re-add its block (their --check warns that the section is missing). Noted in AGENTS.md.
close_reason: AGENTS.md cut from 172 to 43 lines, CLAUDE.md is a one-line @AGENTS.md import

title: Bob Ross example: paint the clouds the way he did
description: The clouds in examples/bob_ross_style.py are built unlike Bob Ross's: three invisible passes lifting the wet blue, the whole body in one long stroke, perfect circles heaped on a ruled flat base, and no blending. They read as flat white cut-outs with no shadowed underside. Rework cloud(): white scrubbed straight onto the wet sky in small circles to make irregular tops, the base blended into the sky with a clean dry brush and fluffed upward, a very light sweep across, each cloud finished before the one in front of it. Script only if possible. Changes the picture: judge by measurements, regenerate all of examples/output/.
close_reason: cloud() in examples/bob_ross_style.py rewritten: white scrubbed onto the wet sky along each billow's top and down, base blended with a clean dry brush (mixing, no pickup), fluffed, one sweep; clouds are layered masses. Measurements in CHANGELOG. All examples regenerated; only bob_ross_style.png changed.

title: Structural clean-up of _engine.py and the stroke runner
description:
The improvement pass merged in PR #14 left `oilpaint/_engine.py` at about 3,900 lines. The code-quality audit's structural findings for the engine and the stroke runner were deferred so they would not collide with the speed work. That work is merged, so they can be done now. This comes first because both remaining paint features (ploughing/marbling, dry-brush over relief) change `brush_step_on`.

Findings still to check against the current code and do (the audit predates the split of `brush.py` into `brush.py`, `stroke.py`, `_knife.py`, `_geometry.py`, `_hair.py`, so find things by name, not by line):

- `_Run.__init__` does five jobs: sampling the stroke, building textures, radii, knife set-up, stroke constants. Split into module-level functions; keep the random-draw order. Drop state that is never read.
- `_Run.step` builds geometry and also spends paint off the canvas. Separate the two.
- `_knife_step` has seven numbered stages in one function. One function per stage; the order the stages change the canvas must stay. Stop passing bare booleans positionally to `lay` and `spread`; fix the misleading parameter names of `flow_under_blade` (`lateral`, `half`).
- `brush_step_on` (cyclomatic complexity about 40): extract njit helpers for the marked stages (drag fraction, column thickness, plough, contact and catch, lay thickness, off-canvas use, stir fraction).
- `footprint`, `level`, `flow_under_blade`, `deposit`: split by phase; replace `deposit`'s three booleans by a mode; one `_bury` helper for the "old top goes under by a share k" loop that is written out in `deposit`, `settle_pending` and `merge_same`.
- `Step` has 38 fields mixing window, motion, hold and carried brush state; the array bundles (`cv`, `aux`, `br`, `taps`, `ridges`, `pend`) are plain tuples read by index. Use nested and named tuples.
- Duplicated helpers (smoothstep, box blur, bilinear sampling, film coverage, Kubelka-Munk `B`/`tau`, per-column demand) and duplicated or unnamed constants (`MIN_FILM`, dab span 1.3, swap rates, volume per amount, `level` iterations, spatter and lighting numbers).
- `brush`/`stroke` code reads `Canvas` private attributes; give `Canvas` a small engine view instead.
- Indirection that hides errors: `_Step.__getattr__`, `Brush.clean()` calling `__init__`, `ALL` built from `globals()`, shared module-level arrays not marked read-only.
acceptance_criteria:
- Painted state stays bit-identical: `python tools/bench.py --compare` against a baseline saved before the change reports all 16 scenes identical.
- Speed within noise of the baseline on `tools/bench.py` (extra array returns and recompiled kernels measured, not assumed).
- `tox` passes (tests, coverage, black, ruff, pyright, spell-check); the ruff complexity exemption for `_engine.py` is removed or narrowed.
notes:
Plan: three stages, each bit-identical against a saved bench baseline. 1) split the oversized kernels in _engine.py; 2) Python side (stroke.py, _knife.py, Canvas engine view, duplicated helpers and constants, indirections); 3) named tuples for Step and the array bundles. Opus 5.5 medium agents implement and review; the orchestrator verifies and merges.
Stage 1 done (commit a1a6de7): every function in _engine.py at or under complexity 13, ruff exemption for the file removed, all 16 bench scenes identical, cold compile 47 s vs 43 s. Split helpers are inline="always". Stage 2 (Python side: stroke.py, _knife.py, Canvas engine view) next.
Stage 2 done: stroke set-up split into module-level functions, knife kernel calls by keyword, Canvas relief maps in one _Relief with read-only view properties (pickle layout unchanged), shared _coverage/_km_terms, engine constants, explicit ALL lists, read-only tables. Paint and renders byte-identical; 587 tests. Stage 3 (named tuples for Step and the array bundles) next.
Stage 3 done (commit e642a7c): Layers/Beneath/Load/Pending/Taps/Ridges named tuples read by field; Step(win, motion, hold); brush_step takes a plain kit once per stroke and names it on entry (numba resolves named tuples more slowly per call). make pre-push passes: tox on py3.11-3.15, wheel, coverage 81.4%, spelling; 589 tests. Not done by decision: deposit keeps its three boolean flags (independent, four combinations in use); settle_pending's and the hold-back's burials stay separate (different arithmetic); StrokeConsts and the chord tables stay flat/plain (per-call cost).
close_reason: All three stages merged on ccr-77a655e0-ewp724: kernels split (complexity <= 13, ruff exemption for _engine.py removed), Python side tidied, bundles and Step named. All 16 bench scenes byte-identical to the pre-change baseline, renders byte-identical, speed within noise, cold compile +8%, tox green on every Python.

title: Ploughing and marbling through thick wet paint
description:
Paint audit mechanism R7, not built in PR #14. A loaded brush pushed hard through thick wet paint should cut grooves into it, leave the old paint standing between the grooves, and lay the new colour into them, which gives the marbled look of wet-in-wet work. Today the brush rides on its own load and stirs the two paints evenly, so about 85-90% of a blue bed is left untouched under a white stroke at pressure 0.9 and the core of the stroke is nearly uniform.

Design from the audit (in `brush_step_on`):
1. Bristle level `gap(p, stiffness)` above the floor, independent of the brush's own load.
2. Cut deeper along clump lines (low `hair`); leave old paint standing between them.
3. The side share of ploughed paint grows with pressure and stiffness (it is a fixed 35% today); lay new paint into the grooves with weight `1 - hair`.
4. Replace `stir` here with a lane-wise fold: full exchange in groove lanes, none in ridge lanes.

Apply only above about pressure 0.4 and on wet paint thicker than about 1.5 units, so that "white over wet sky stays white" survives.
acceptance_criteria:
- Blue left under a white stroke at pressure 0.9: under 60% (today about 85-90%), with ridges at least 1.3x the bed.
- Luminance standard deviation across the stroke core at pressure 0.6 and above: at least 0.08 and rising with pressure (today 0.024-0.026).
- Regression scenes `blending`, `dirty_brush` and the Bob Ross example checked by metrics and amplified difference images, not by eye alone.
- Pigment is conserved; `tox` passes; speed measured with `tools/bench.py`.
notes: First implementation (worktree branch, 3 commits) met the audit's white-hog-flat criteria but was sent back, not merged: across 11 presets it leaves the same few hard-edged pin-stripes (film or bare, not marbled), is not monotonic in stiffness (BRIGHT streaks less than FLAT_HOG), lanes don't scale with brush width, streak measure varies 0.033-0.208 by seed, and the gates were windowed around presets and one example (mixing gate). Rework asked for: response continuous and monotonic in stiffness with no preset-shaped windows and no mixing gate; lanes in proportion to the hair field from every clump, no threshold; partial mixing so the visible layer holds tints; per-pixel locality; total laid unchanged. New acceptance is measured over >=5 seeds and several brushes (stiffness sweep, seed robustness, not two-valued, lane count scaling with width, locality).
close_reason: Ploughing and marbling implemented as a general behaviour of paint and hair (pressure, thickness, body, stiffness, hair pattern, mixing); reviewed twice; 624 tests, coverage 81.5%; wide-brush ridge shape left to oilpaint-qmz

title: Wide brushes' side ridges are still steeper than a small brush's
description:
After oilpaint-qmz a brush's side ridges may grow with the brush past 7 px (room = 0.12*w_typ*(1+spread)+1), which removed the black wall beside a 120 px stroke. The room grows linearly with the brush while the paint pushed aside grows faster, so the proportions of a 36 px brush are not kept: width at half height / (0.6 * height) is 1.01 at 36 px, 0.53 at 70 px, 0.40 at 120 px (protocol: white hog flat at p 0.9, amount 45*w/36, down 5 units of wet blue; 5 seeds). Slope of a 120 px ridge about 7 units/px against level's yield slope of about 4 for tube paint.

Also left alone by oilpaint-qmz: (1) the bead where a wide brush sets down keeps the 7 px cap (margin - 1); (2) with a 120 px flat and a very heavy load on bare canvas, 14 of 438 outer edge pixels holding >0.8 units come out paler than full paint (main: none), because the wider ridge's last pixel is partly covered and settling then fills it.

Constraints found the hard way (see oilpaint-qmz notes): a ridge whose width follows the paint step by step makes the outer edge wander and breaks either test_the_level_edge_of_heavy_paint_stays_solid or test_stroke_edges_are_anti_aliased; a slump to the yield slope gives wide pale slabs and halos on bare canvas and costs 20-47%. Judge any change by renders first (scripts protocol.py / heavy_bare.py described in oilpaint-qmz).
notes: Stage 2 + fix round 1 (worktree 53e3a97, candidate on the branch): review 1 findings fixed (pick share per pixel: only the sideways escape is limited; set-down to the ring; ramp coverage its own pass cover_ramps on own top paint, idempotent, gated on the lateral footprint; exact column depth for turned brushes; Rembrandt soften() tests the mop's path - beret band gone). My verification of 53e3a97: static clean, 735 passed + 1 xfailed, coverage 81.78%, bench round-small/knife/edges/stipple identical, all example images regenerate identically. Review 2: no correctness/conservation bug; fixes wanted in tests (single-seed bounds), text (anti-aliasing cost understated), a float nit at s=1, soften() centreline only, gate-blend mutants. Fix round 2 with the implementer, including one time-boxed trial: tell a level edge from a slant by the coverage gradient along the edge so the ramp pass costs less anti-aliasing. Accepted trade-offs so far: clean wide brush picks up ~1/3 more over a stroke; bead still 1.3-1.6x the side ridges at 120 px; 120 px heavy level edge still partly pale (strict xfail + bound).
close_reason: Paint deep under a wide brush is held back: squeezed paint stays on the brush, ploughed paint stays unlifted in its layer; only paint within 20 px of the footprint's nearer edge escapes freely (EDGE_FREE, EDGE_SQUEEZE). 120 px protocol ridges 17-20 units instead of 40-47, proportions of a 36 px brush; bead 23 instead of 54. Slope cover (cover_ramps) on the stroke's own edge paint, idempotent, leaves slanting edges' anti-aliasing. Two independent reviews and a delta review; 738 tests + 1 xfail; all example images regenerated (Rembrandt soften() now tests the mop's footprint). Left open: see the follow-up issue (bead height, palest level-edge feet).

title: Side ridges of a wide brush stand too tall and narrow
description: The paint a brush pushes out to its sides is laid within the stroke's margin, which stroke.py caps at 8 px. For a wide brush the ridge's width therefore stops growing while the volume moved keeps growing, so the ridge stands implausibly tall and reads as a dark outline in the lit render. Measured with ploughing (oilpaint-e5s), white at pressure 0.9 through about 5 units of wet blue: ridge height above the bed 3.3 units at 16 px (half-height width 3.7 px), 9.4 at 36 px (5.5 px), 23 at 70 px (7.3 px); before ploughing the 70 px brush already gave 11.6. A ridge 23 units high and 7 px wide is steeper than the yield slope of the stiffest paint (about 4 units per px). Wanted: the side ridge's width grows with the volume it holds (or it slumps to the paint's yield slope as it is laid), so that height stays plausible for any brush width. This widens the window of every stroke, so every bench scene will change and the cost must be measured.
notes:
Design decision (orchestrator, from renders): do not slump the ridge to level's yield slope as it is laid. Slumped ridges become wide pale flat banks with a sharp outline (tape beside the stroke), puddles and flanges on bare canvas, +20-47% cost on heavy strokes. Chosen design: main's shape law unchanged (w = 1.2 sqrt(area), about as high as wide), with the width limited by a room of about 0.3 x the mark's width instead of margin - 1 (7 px); bead, knives and dabs as on main. Strokes whose ridges stay under the old cap are byte-identical.
Design decision, final: the uncapped width law made the ridge's edge wander from step to step, which no ending of its last pixel reconciles with both test_the_level_edge_of_heavy_paint_stays_solid and test_stroke_edges_are_anti_aliased (main passes both because the capped width is constant along a stroke). Final design: main's ridge unchanged, but its cap grows with the brush at every width: room = max(margin, 0.12 * w_typ * (1 + spread) + 1), side ridge w clipped to room - 1; bead, knives, dabs as on main. Brushes under the knee (hog flat up to about 55 px) are byte-identical to main. The set-down bead of a wide brush keeps the 7 px cap (not addressed here).
close_reason: A brush's side ridges may grow with the brush past 7 px (room = margin's rule without its upper clip); the black wall beside a 120 px stroke is gone. Strokes whose margin never reached the clip are byte-identical; all 16 bench scenes identical; 640 tests. Proportions only partly restored (120 px: 0.19 -> 0.40 against 1.01 at 36 px); remainder filed as a follow-up.

title: tools/bench.py --compare does not cover the rendered picture
description: tools/bench.py --save/--compare fingerprints the painted state (wet layers, coverage, dried height, relief maps, rng state, stroke counter, brush loads) but never renders. A change confined to canvas compositing, spectral.py or _render.py therefore passes --compare whatever it does to the picture. In oilpaint-b63 stage 2 the rendering side had to be proved with a one-off script that compared render(), reflectance(), color_at(), surface_height() and the Kubelka-Munk functions between two trees. To do: let the bench also record, per scene, the bytes of the lit and unlit render and of surface_height() (as extra keys in the saved state or behind a flag such as --render, so the timing of the painting itself is not disturbed), and compare them bytewise like the rest. Keep old saved states comparable or say clearly that they must be re-saved.
acceptance_criteria: A deliberate one-bit change in _render.shade or canvas compositing is reported by --compare; the painting timings are unaffected by the extra work; CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md convention line still holds as written.
close_reason: tools/bench.py --save/--compare record and compare seven picture arrays per scene (lit, unlit, raking and overhead lamps, absorbent ground, reflectance, surface height) after the timed loop. A nudged constant in _render.shade is reported as a picture difference with exit 1; old-format states compare the paint and say the picture was not compared. Empty selections and self-comparison are refused. Still unrendered by the 16 scenes: lit reverse paintings (lighting is skipped there by design) and a few branches in _render.py (zero blur radius, the low-lamp limit).

title: Cached render kernels can go stale when spectral.py changes
description: numba's on-disk cache for a kernel is keyed on the modification time and size of the kernel's own source file, and globals from other modules are frozen into the compiled code. _render.py compiles N_BANDS from spectral.py into its cached kernels with no guard of its own; the _compiled_packed check in _engine.py only protects _render when _engine.py is unchanged. If spectral.WAVELENGTHS (and so N_BANDS) changes without _render.py changing, a stale cached kernel could be loaded. Found in the review of oilpaint-b63 stage 2 (which is why _dab.SPAN duplicates _engine.DAB_SPAN, pinned by a test). To do: list every cross-module global read inside a cached kernel (_engine.py, _render.py, _dab.py and any other njit code), and give each either a local copy pinned by a test or a guard like _compiled_packed that fails loudly when the compiled value differs from the current one.
acceptance_criteria: Every global from another module used inside a cache=True kernel is either duplicated locally with an equality test or checked at import against the compiled value; a test demonstrates the guard for _render.
close_reason: The band count is a literal in _engine.py and _render.py, checked at import against spectral.N_BANDS (an edit of the kernel file is what makes numba drop its cache), and each kernel file keeps a tiny cached guard kernel for a cache that kept its stamp all the same (numba < 0.68 with a preserved file time; stale bytecode). Audit: the band count was the only cross-module value compiled into a cached kernel; a test now checks no kernel reads a name from another oilpaint module. Known limits: numba's own index-then-data save is not atomic; the guard was run on numba 0.68.1 only.

title: Dry-brush should catch dried crests and skip the hollows
description:
Paint audit mechanism R11, not built in PR #14. A nearly dry brush dragged lightly over dried impasto should leave paint only on the crests it touches and skip the hollows (scumbling). Today the deposit does not follow dried relief at furrow scale: the correlation between a scumble and the dry relief under it is -0.14.

Design from the audit:
- Give the tips a height: `tip_level = local mean surface + reach(p, stiffness)`; scale the deposit by how far a point lies below it, more strongly at low pressure and low load.
- This needs a second "below local mean" map at furrow scale (blur 4-6 px) beside `_hollows` in `canvas.py`, rebuilt at `dry()`.
- Confine it to pressure under about 0.35.
acceptance_criteria:
- Correlation between scumble deposit and the dry relief under it: at least +0.3 (today -0.14).
- Strokes at pressure 0.35 and above are unchanged (bit-identical on the scenes that do not scumble).
- `tox` passes; speed measured with `tools/bench.py`.
notes: Stage 1 (2026-11-12): the defect is real. On the default canvas a nearly dry or moderately loaded brush at p 0.1-0.3 over dried hog impasto lays a solid opaque patch (crests and furrows alike), then runs dry; the audit's -0.14 reproduces. Cause: _catch's threshold is <= 0 while a column still holds paint (fill above ~0.5), so every pixel catches whatever tooth says; rough_thr is 0 on the default canvas. The tooth map itself is fine (+0.96 with the dried relief) and the whole-canvas normalisation is not the culprit. Prototype (35 lines): a catch factor from how far a point lies below the brush's reach, reach = 3 p^2 (1.6 - stiffness); r(volume, relief) at p 0.1 goes -0.01 -> +0.51 on hog impasto, -0.22 -> +0.26 on knife slabs; bare canvas bit-identical; 14 of 16 bench scenes identical. Decisions for stage 2: no cut at p 0.35 (continuous in pressure; the issue's bit-identity criterion above 0.35 is dropped), reach also grows with the load on the tips, depth measured from the real surface beyond a weave allowance (existing hollows map if it serves), and the catch made ragged with the hair and tooth instead of crisp bars.
close_reason: Landed as a reach of the brush tips below the dried surface (pressure, softness, load): r(volume laid, dried relief) at p 0.1 over hog impasto -0.01 -> +0.42; bare canvas and flat films byte-identical; 15/16 bench scenes identical, painting 0.07% of pixels > 1/255; 22 tests in tests/test_scumble.py, each failing under a named mutant. The issue's criterion 'bit-identical at p >= 0.35' was dropped: the reach is continuous in pressure; strokes at p >= 0.5 cover as before, at p 0.3 with the default load the hollows covered go 0.56 -> 0.51. Not covered by tests: wet paint lying in dried hollows, dabs and stipple over relief.

title: Colour bands of a double-loaded brush should wander with the furrows
description:
A double-loaded brush (two or more colours side by side on the tip) lays straight colour bands, while the furrows left by the hairs wander, merge and split along the stroke since PR #14. The colour boundaries should follow the same 2-D hair field as the relief, so that the bands drift with the furrows instead of running ruler-straight through them.

Best done together with ploughing and marbling, which reworks how lanes exchange paint.
notes: Design direction (2026-11-12): the general mechanism, not a gate on multi-loading: for a brush stroke the place across the mark that bristle_taps sees is displaced by the hair field's own sideways drift (same lattices, no new rng draws), for laying and pick-up alike. Evenly loaded strokes will change slightly too. Two stages: prototype with renders and numbers first, judged before any polish (lesson of oilpaint-qmz). Before-state of main 68a8873 saved with tools/bench.py --save.
close_reason: Not built: a prototype showed the fix as filed is invisible and not worth what it disturbs. Measured on main 68a8873 (two-colour strokes, 5 seeds): the hair's sideways drift is sd ~0.9 px (max ~2.7 px) for hogs, 0.4 px for sable, whatever the brush width; the colour boundary of a multi-loaded stroke is a gradient about 20 px wide at default blending. A prototype that displaced the bristle columns by the hair's own drift (branch worktree-agent-a9c408ffc2b472076, commit 3f65159) made boundary and furrow move together (correlation +0.94 to +0.99, ratio ~1) with no visible difference at sheet scale and a 1-2 px wobble at 3x with blending 0.05. It changed every brush scene slightly (1-32% of pixels over 1/255), broke four reach tests on thin brushes (a px-sized drift is 4-10 columns on a liner or an 8 px flat) and cost +1.3%. What makes furrows look as if they wander is merging, splitting and fading, which columns cannot follow. If double-loaded strokes are to look less smooth at the boundary, that is a different feature (clump-scale streaking of the two colours), to be judged from renders first.

title: Lifted multi-colour dab drifts a few percent in one pigment
description:
Known limit left by PR #14: when a brush loaded with several colours is dabbed and lifted, the amount of one pigment can end up a few percent off what the brush gave up. Single-colour dabs and drawn strokes conserve pigment.

Find where the lift-off or the dab mound shares paint between colours without conserving each pigment separately (`_lift_off`, dab mounds), and add a conservation test for a multi-colour dab.
notes: Stage 1 (measured): the drift is all in the two lift steps (stroke._dab_lift and _knife._lift_off scale each pixel's paint by a factor that keeps total volume only). Up to 19% of a K band for heavy three-colour dabs, 1e-3..1e-2 for lighter loads, 6e-4..3e-3 for knives; mound and the rest conserve to 1e-8. Fix: local transport (engine kernel pull_up: symmetric Gaussian plan, 4 Sinkhorn passes, pool for the remainder, every pixel ends with V*fac), conserving to 4e-8. Decisions for stage 2: keep that design and its sigmas; fall back to scaling where the stroke's own paint is uniform (single-colour marks keep bytes and speed); peak colour now comes from its neighbours (accepted).
close_reason: Lifted dabs and knives now move paint (engine kernel pull_up: local Sinkhorn plan over a square window, remainder through a pool) instead of scaling each pixel; every channel kept to float32 rounding (worst 3.6e-8 of what the brush gave up, was up to 0.2). Two independent reviews, 25 mutants killed. Known: 18-47% of a dab's moved paint and 4-19% of a knife's is shared over the whole mark's rising pixels rather than taken from nearby; pull_up costs about 20 ms on a 200 px three-colour dab.

title: Wide brushes: the set-down bead is still taller than the side ridges, and the palest level-edge feet remain
description: Left open by oilpaint-mtm. (1) At 120 px the bead where a wide brush is set down still stands 1.3x (on wet paint) to 1.6x (bare canvas) the height of its side ridges; letting the bead's width grow to room - 1 was tried and gave a broad pale cap with bulging corners. (2) On a heavy 120 px level edge 12% (3-19% over five strokes) of the outer pixels holding over a unit still come out paler than the stroke, the palest by about 135 levels, as on main; tests/test_wide.py records it as a strict xfail plus a bound. The slope cover (cover_ramps) leaves feet between unlike neighbours alone so that slanting edges keep their anti-aliasing, which is why uneven runs stay pale. Judge any change by multi-seed tables (anti-aliasing columns and pale share) and renders, as in oilpaint-mtm's notes.
notes: Stage 1: bead's '1.3-1.6x' was mostly a measuring artefact; real defect a notch at every corner (side ridges start at step 2). Pale feet: the ridge's paint reaches half a px past its coverage; level/soften slump more in. Stage 2 (worktree agent-aa8162bd4fe63ce2a, cd33bf6; candidate on the branch, main with PR #25 merged in and bob_ross_style.png regenerated): A (RIDGE_COVER: ridge covers as far as its paint reaches) kept gated to wide footprints (ungated it fattens thin strokes by up to 0.5 px and costs anti-aliasing); B1 (set-down squeeze split: the share a normal step would squeeze goes to the sides) ungated, knives and dabs excluded; cover_ramps kept (without it a pale fringe along the whole edge). Three pale-share tests replaced by smoothness/corner/bead tests. My verification of cd33bf6: static clean, 757 passed, coverage 81.78%, examples regenerate identically. Review: merge after fixes - engine right, conservation holds, no cost; fixes in tests (bead-ratio test over-fitted to seeds, ridge-cover test passes on main, tautological gate test, notch bound flaky, no end-to-end guard against a pale band) and text (false 'fewer a lot paler' claim, wrong bead ratios); plus the corner on wet paint still half a notch (ploughed share at touchdown all goes to the bead) and _geo's inner cut-off moved. Fix round with the implementer.
close_reason: Bead: the 1.3-1.6x figure was mostly a measuring artefact; the real defect was a notch at each corner. Side ridges now start where the brush is set down (squeeze and plough at set-down split as any step would; knives, dabs, stipples untouched): just past the bead the side ridge stands 0.84/0.99/1.02 of its steady height at 36/70/120 px down wet paint (main 0.17/0.34/0.46) and 1.05/1.02/0.99 on bare canvas (0.79/0.55/0.56). Pale feet: a wide brush's side ridge now covers as far as its paint reaches (RIDGE_COVER, gated to wide footprints); level edges are smoothly anti-aliased where they were notched (roughness 0.113 against 0.156), slanted heavy edges lose their sawtooth; cover_ramps kept. Pale-share tests replaced by smoothness, pale-band, corner and bead-height tests set by 30-seed bootstraps. Known and documented: down wet paint a small brush's stroke starts flush, without a bead; more edge pixels count as pale (softer edge, same darkness summed across it); gated cover costs up to 2 of 120 anti-aliased columns at 36 px.

title: One-pixel crests at shallow slants still bead in the highlights
description: Known limit left by PR #14: highlights are now gathered along narrow crests, but a crest that is one pixel wide and runs at a shallow slant to the pixel grid still shows as a string of beads at the pixel steps instead of a continuous glint.
notes: Stage 2 (8062932, candidate on the branch): reach grows towards one step of the staircase on shallow crests that run on (GLOSS_SPAN_MAX 16, RUN_ON (20, 8)); my verification passed (766 tests, bench state byte-identical, examples identical). Attempts dropped: 0.3 px crests (opens the gate on weave/dabs/stipple/spatter); low crests (helps synthetic painted ridges, nothing visible on real marks, whose curvature gate is already open). Independent review: merge after fixes - works in scope (beading -40..75% at 2-15 deg, neutral from 20, untouched things untouched, ring buffers proven against a no-wrap oracle) but: (1) a point glint at a crossing/T-junction/knob on a straight crest is smeared into detached streaks (_runs_on reads only the two ends), teardrop spatter glints stretched; (2) _crest's direction is biased towards 45 deg for thin crests, so the long reach drifts off the crest: 196 of 17,391 sweep cases worse by >0.01, brightness not conserved (0.91-1.15); (3) noisy reach on knobbly paint makes lone sparkles, a pixel inside a spatter drop gains 16 levels; (4) jumps where the tap count changes; text claims overstated (exactly-as-before only for smooth crests; +5-10% render time on crest-dense pictures). Fix round with the implementer; bar: no new artefact class against main, else revert and document.

title: A few footprint-edge pixels are still sensitive to rounding
description:
Known limit left by PR #14: under a clean brush or knife, a few pixels at the edge of the footprint can still flip between covered and empty depending on rounding in the last bit (for example between CPUs). PR #14 removed most of this by making coverage use the `EMPTY` threshold; the remaining cases are at footprint edges.

Low priority: the effect is a handful of pixels and is not visible in renders, but it limits bit-exact comparison across machines.
